name: LightSim reference suite
about: Real vehicles with official test results, run through LightSim and compared automatically (VAL-05). README.md explains the rules; backend/tests/test_reference_suite.py runs it in CI.

rules.test_mass: equivalent test weight (EPA's dynamometer inertia setting), lb x 0.45359237 kg
rules.rotating_inertia_note: EPA ALPHA's convention, simulated inertia = test weight x 1.015, all of it put in the four wheels; motor, gear and brake inertias are 0
rules.road_load: EPA target coefficients A, B, C (lbf, lbf/mph, lbf/mph^2) x 4.448222, x 2.763930, x 1.717157 to N, N/(km/h), N/(km/h)^2, with Coefficients Include Driveline Losses ticked so the final drive and differential run lossless
rules.overall_ratio: EPA's N/V ratio (motor 1/min per mph) turned into the gear ratio for the wheel radius: ratio = N/V x 2 pi r / (60 x 0.44704)
rules.motor_loss: FASTSim's efficiency against output power (as % of the motor's power): loss = P / eff - P, the same for driving and recuperating; no loss at zero power and no drag torque, so the spin losses the road load holds are not counted twice
rules.motor_power: EPA's Rated Horsepower (Test Car List) x 0.7457 kW where the case gives it (rated_hp), else FASTSim's motor power (motor_kW)
rules.motor_full_load: constant torque up to a third of the maximum speed, then the motor's power; maximum speed = N/V x 110 mph
rules.battery: a flat 350 V open-circuit voltage; internal resistance giving 1.5 % loss at a 1C discharge (FASTSim's 97 % round trip split each way): R = 0.015 x 350^2 / (kWh x 1000)
rules.wall_energy: (net energy at the battery terminals + the battery's internal losses) / charger efficiency, per km of the cycle driven; the charger efficiency is FASTSim's 0.86, uncertain by +/- 0.04
rules.mpge_to_wh_per_km: 33,705 Wh per US gallon equivalent / (mpge x 1.609344 km per mile)
